Vitalik Buterin said Ethereum should focus more on ETH as a store of value rather than as a “fee-burning token,” arguing that fee burn was never as strong a valuation floor as it appeared and that maximizing fees could conflict with decentralization and capture resistance.

A Paris criminal court sentenced a former Holograph Foundation employee to five years in prison, with two years to be served and three years suspended, for illegally minting 1 billion HLG tokens worth approximately $14 million in 2024. The defendant manipulated token minting conditions and transferred the tokens to personal wallets, working with two accomplices to move the proceeds through crypto exchanges.

Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Has Remained Below Its ATH for 374 Consecutive Days, Setting an All-Time Record

Bitcoin's mining difficulty has spent 374 consecutive days below its all-time high of 155.97 T (set on October 29, 2025), officially marking the longest such stretch in the network's history and surpassing the previous 364-day record from the 2011 crash as well as the 253-day gap following China's 2021 mining ban. The protracted plateau is driven by muted BTC price action (~$76,000) and escalating overhead, prompting publicly listed miners to liquidate Bitcoin reserves and pivot site power toward AI colocation. — link

acb2b787a644.tgtext:
U.S. Sanctions Eight Canadian Crypto Firms Over Iran-Linked Transactions

The U.S. Treasury sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses on November 6, including NIA Nations, Million Exchange, Amin Exchange and Farah Exchange, saying they facilitated cross-border transactions involving Iran through digital assets. Treasury said several of the firms transacted with sanctioned Iranian crypto exchanges or addresses linked to the IRGC, while some also helped launder drug proceeds for Canadian trafficker Ryan Wedding by converting cash into digital assets and sending the funds abroad.

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT said he had publicly called for sanctions against Iran-linked OTC brokers in Canada five months earlier. — link
